finds.quote: What they share is the condition under which the classical object is met: non-possession. The text, the beloved and the dead are each reached across what keeps them from being had whole.
finds.falsifier_quote: A reader may also judge the determination of §2: whether the class nouns only compress, and whether "playful" replaces the relation the work bears at its classical loci. A reading that finds "playful dialogue" the right name for that relation, with grounds at *If Not, Winter*, *Eros the Bittersweet* and *Nox*, is a successful reading, appended as a disagreement with the determination
finds.window: Carson's works at their classical loci: If Not, Winter (2002), Eros the Bittersweet (1986), Nox (2010)
finds.note: Reading of what Carson's work does at its classical loci, argued from three loci; §6.2 states what reading would count against it.

finds.quote: "Playful" substitutes the governing modality of the relation: a relation conditioned by what cannot be had is represented as a relation characterized by what the artist does with an available tradition. A reader who has only the sentence will reconstruct a relation of play with antiquity, and the reconstruction is accurate to one register of the work, which is what makes the replacement hold.
finds.falsifier_quote: L8 is what makes the determination checkable by anyone: the loss the sentence drops is recovered by the same body's text of the same day.
finds.note: The determination that 'playful' liquidates the relation: a thesis about what a text (the 2026 motivation) does in reception; checkable via the biobibliography (L8). Includes a conditional claim about what readers of the sentence will reconstruct.

finds.quote: The relation the work bears to the classical tradition, on this specification, is to the text *as transmitted*: quoted, damaged, lost, translated, and surviving in the form of its survival.
finds.note: Thesis that Carson's relation is to the classical text as transmitted; summarizes O1–O5.

finds.quote: O4 is stated at what Carson adds: the figure becomes the book's centre and its life is told whole. If a reading of the fragments finds that they already give Geryon a whole life, O4 is revised.
finds.falsifier_quote: If a reading of the fragments finds that they already give Geryon a whole life, O4 is revised.
finds.note: O4 as a thesis about what Carson added to Stesichoros, with its own revision condition.

finds.quote: The archive predicted it. #1587: "composers asked about this packet will tend to restate it as 'closely related authors' or 'a school,' and the archive will record the restatements as data" (T1587-07); "'shared school', 'master and pupil', 'editorial overlap' … Each of those is a *cushion*: a phrase that lets the received two-author model absorb the finding without answering it" (T1587-04). The archive's own composer fulfilled the prediction.

finds.quote: 1. "Theophrastus" is the name under which part of one corpus has come down, the corpus transmitted under the names Aristotle and Theophrastus, which the surviving texts do not support dividing into two distinct authors; how many made it is open, because it has not been counted. `T1587-01 T1588-01 T1588-03 T1587-02`
finds.falsifier_quote: an epigraphic or papyrological witness outside the manuscript tradition, a second voice marked at the hinge, or an extant work under this name answering the fragment's questions would each weaken it, and none is held.
finds.note: Authorship thesis: one corpus under two names, maker count open; composed as the knowledge object's first sentence with stated weakeners.

finds.quote: The person the received account describes is built from receiving texts. Diogenes Laertius, five centuries later, gives the parentage and the city on another writer's authority ("Theophrastus, son of Melantas, of Eresus, a fuller's son, as Athenodorus says"), the hearing of Plato and then of Aristotle, the succession to the school when Aristotle withdrew to Chalcis, two thousand pupils, a life of eighty-five years, and the change of the name Tyrtamus to Theophrastus by Aristotle "for the divine quality of his speech", which Strabo also reports.
finds.falsifier_quote: Guard: "The ledger does not show that Plato or Theophrastus were not persons; it shows what the attestation of persons rests on" (T1658-08).
finds.note: Thesis that the biographical Theophrastus is constructed by receiving texts (ρ = constructs).

finds.quote: 9. That Aristotle handed his library to Theophrastus is Strabo's, three centuries on; Aristotle's will names no books, and no text states how they passed. Strabo also carries the story of the books buried at Scepsis, which the received account offers for the corruption of the texts, and through that one channel both corpora reach us. `F6 F10 T1581-07 T1581-08 T165-01 T1570-04`
finds.window: Strabo XIII.1.54; Aristotle's will, DL V.11–16
finds.note: Historical claim: the library transfer rests on Strabo alone; Aristotle's will names no books.

finds.quote: At the short Metaphysics, also called On First Principles, the corpus shows its seam: the sixth and seventh sections are written from inside Λ, with no sign at the hinge of a second voice; at 5a21–23 the fragment names Λ 8's object, the number of the spheres, and refuses by name the astronomers' method Λ uses; a directed measure of rare-term uptake ranks the edge from the fragment to Λ first of 1,482; which was written first, the sequence cannot decide.
finds.window: Theophrastus, Metaphysics 6–7 and Aristotle Metaphysics Λ
finds.note: Thesis on the seam between Theophrastus's Metaphysics and Λ; priority of composition left undecided.

finds.quote: The doxography through which the Presocratics are known descends through this name and Aristotle's, and all four kinds of witness to the received division of Plato from Aristotle pass through it.
finds.note: Thesis about the transmission route of the doxography and of the received Plato/Aristotle division.

finds.quote: The received figure "less than a tenth survives" relates two acts, a list and a transmission, and does not measure a loss. `F9 F29 F61 T1581-06`
finds.note: Claim that the 'less than a tenth survives' figure does not measure a loss; borderline H (methodological reading of a historical figure).
